metabolic-rate.def: The rate at which the body uses energy, and so makes heat. The basal metabolic rate (BMR), measured awake at rest after a 12-hour fast in a warm room, is about 60 to 70% of the total metabolic rate, which also includes handling food and physical activity.

energy-balance.def: The relation between energy taken in as food and energy spent. A positive balance is stored, mostly as fat; a negative balance draws stores down. Body mass index (kg/m²) screens body weight, and dietary guidelines give official advice on healthy eating.

appetite.def: The control of hunger and eating by the hypothalamus. Ghrelin from the empty stomach raises hunger; stomach stretch and gut hormones produce satiety, the fullness that ends a meal; leptin from fat reports long-term stores.

core-temperature.def: The temperature of the deep tissues (brain, chest and abdominal organs), held near 36.6 to 37 °C, as opposed to the shell of skin and limbs, whose temperature varies widely with blood flow and surroundings.

thermoregulation.def: Control of core temperature by the preoptic area of the hypothalamus, which matches heat loss to heat production: skin vasodilation and sweating when warm; skin vasoconstriction, shivering and nonshivering thermogenesis in brown fat when cold.

heat-cold-illness.def: Illness when temperature control is overwhelmed. Hyperthermia (heat gain beyond heat loss) ranges from heat exhaustion, with a normal brain, to heat stroke, a core above about 40 °C with brain dysfunction. Hypothermia is a core below 35 °C; frostbite is frozen tissue.
